title: The Lord is my shepherd
hook: green pastures, still waters, the valley of the shadow (Psalm 23)
tomorrow: what does 'be still' mean when the whole world is shaking?

segments.voice: Yesterday, what is man: small under the stars, and crowned with glory anyway. Today, a psalm sung by someone who'd spent nights under those stars with a flock.

On a greeting card, shepherding looks gentle: soft lambs, green hills. The Bible's shepherd boy tells it differently. Young David tells King Saul what he fought off to save one lamb, in the King James Version: "Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock." He went after it, he says, and pulled the lamb out of its mouth.
screen: `SOFT LAMBS ON A GREETING CARD.` → `A LION, AND A BEAR.` → `THE LAMB PULLED OUT OF ITS MOUTH.`

segments.voice: Psalm 23 is headed a psalm of David. So the one who knows what a shepherd risks is now singing as a sheep: "The LORD is my shepherd." Green pastures, still waters, and then the turn: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me." Today's question: who stays with you in the dark valley? The psalm's answer isn't that the valley never comes. It's company. Thou art with me. Many Jewish and Christian families read it at gravesides and hospital beds. It doesn't explain the dark; it walks through it beside you. Now a neighbor who shares the shepherd, in its own words. In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, says God sent no prophet who did not herd sheep. Asked about himself, he says yes, he herded them too, for the people of Mecca. Shared: the shepherd as the picture of care, learned with a flock before it's given to people. And the honest difference. In Psalm 23, the LORD is the shepherd and the singer is the sheep. In the hadith, the prophets are the shepherds, trained by flocks to care for people. One image, held from two sides.

segments.voice: Read the whole psalm once, slowly, from any Bible or a screen, aloud if you can. If it isn't near, say verse four slowly: "Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me." Then let the words settle like water going still.
The Lord is my shepherd: the first line of Psalm 23, sung by a shepherd as a sheep, with company promised in the valley.

howItsDone: Jews and Christians pray Psalm 23 at funerals, at bedsides and in daily prayer; in some Jewish homes it is sung at the third Sabbath meal. Muslims honor the prophets, including David (Dawud) and Muhammad, as shepherds who herded sheep.

chat.says: theo asked me to read psalm 23 with him at his grandma's grave sunday. does it promise nothing bad happens?
options: No. It walks into the dark valley; the promise is company: thou art with me.
Yes. If you trust the shepherd, the dark valley never comes.
It promises green pastures after death, not help along the way.
chat.meaning: Psalm 23 doesn't skip the valley of the shadow of death. Its promise is presence: I will fear no evil, for thou art with me.

tie.story: David, who fought a lion for one lamb, sings as a sheep: in the dark valley, thou art with me.
